meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to believe', paired with 'верить'.

examples.text: Со своего телефона? И все поверили?
examples.trans: From your own phone? And everyone believed it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А зачем? Я сам сделал так, чтобы он его написал.
examples.trans: And why would I? I'm the one who made him write it.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'схитительный'). Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('delightful, admirable, delicious').

examples.trans: The food in the restaurant is simply delicious.

examples.text: Он назвал всю нашу еду просто восхитительной!
examples.trans: He called all our food simply delicious!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('glad').

examples.trans: I'm very glad to see you.

examples.text: Ну что ты? Я очень рад тебя видеть.
examples.trans: Oh, come on! I'm very glad to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нравиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be liked, to please', paired with 'нравиться'.

examples.trans: Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

examples.text: А придётся! Не бойся, тебе понравится.
examples.trans: Well, you'll have to! Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to thank', paired with 'поблагодарить'.

examples.text: Всё, не благодари меня. И с Аникеевым реши.
examples.trans: That's it, don't thank me. And sort out Anikeev.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

переживать.gloss: to worry, to fret; to go through

meanings.en: to worry, to fret; to go through
meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'живать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry, to fret; to go through', paired with 'пережить'.

examples.trans: Why are you worrying like that?
Don't worry, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Что вы так переживаете? Самсонов всё, он себя закопал.
examples.trans: Why are you worrying like that? Samsonov is finished, he buried himself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'рядок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order.

examples.text: Теперь давай всё по порядку. Скажи мне, сколько ты им должна?
examples.trans: Now let's go through everything in order. Tell me, how much do you owe them?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello, hey', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Алло, Танечка! В свои годы это нормально.
examples.trans: Hello, Tanechka! At my age that's normal.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, back then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'третиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to meet', paired with 'встречаться'.

examples.text: Аркаша, губернатор хочет с нами встретиться!
examples.trans: Arkasha, the governor wants to meet with us!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in (time); through', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'hour' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in an hour.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'over, above; at', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The lamp is above the table.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'stop', paired with 'останавливать'.

examples.text: Лицо у тебя побито, Ваня! Ты хулиганов остановил в ресторане!
examples.trans: Your face is beaten up, Vanya! You stopped hooligans in the restaurant!
You stopped hooligans in the restaurant!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Подожди, там же в марте холодно!
examples.trans: Hold on, it's cold there in March!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Разговорчики, лейтенант Соколов! Быстро на рабочее место.
examples.trans: That's enough talk, Lieutenant Sokolov! Back to your desk, quickly.

отойти.gloss: to step back, to move away

meanings.en: to step back, to move away
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to step back, to move away', paired with 'отходить'.

examples.trans: He stepped over to the window.
Step back! No comment! No comment!
